method: Independent all-string semantic, grammar and script review. Read all 50 unique-source groups per profile; checked all 63 leaves, 11 booleans and repeated-source consistency. No external MT or translation API used.

reviewed.latinProfileSemanticEquivalence: all 63 text leaves preserve the reviewed Latin wording

findings.before: Este proceso é automático. En breve redirixirémosche ao teu destino.
findings.after: Este proceso é automático. En breve redirixirémoste ao teu destino.
findings.assessment: Redirixir takes the person redirected as direct object. Replaced indirect-object che with direct-object te in the future verb, matching the later redirixirte wording.

findings.before: თქვენს IP მისამართს სერვერთან უჩვეულოდ ბევრი კავშირი აქვს
findings.after: თქვენს IP მისამართს სერვერთან კავშირების უჩვეულო რაოდენობა აქვს
findings.assessment: The previous wording stated an abnormally large number of connections. English states only an abnormal number. Replaced the comparative quantity claim with a neutral unusual count, retaining the absence of any confirmed-attack claim.

findings.before: Hic situs per HTTPS adiri potest. Per HTTP conectere conatus es; nunc te redirigere conabimur. Nisi redirigeris, adde https:// initio inscriptionis tuae URL et iterum tenta.
findings.after: Hic situs per HTTPS adiri potest. Per HTTP te conectere conatus es; nunc te redirigere conabimur. Nisi redirigeris, adde https:// initio inscriptionis tuae URL et iterum tenta.
findings.assessment: Added the reflexive object te to transitive conectere, explicitly conveying the user attempting to connect themself and avoiding an assumed intransitive Neo-Latin extension.

languageAssessments.notes: Recognizably Scottish Gaelic, with plausible lenition, prepositional and subordinate-clause forms. Technical browser/server/domain vocabulary and semantics are coherent. Further fluent review of idiom is useful.
Welsh mutation, possessives and verbal constructions are defensible. Origin server, availability, timeout and maintenance expectations remain faithful.
Galician vocabulary and morphology are coherent after repairing the direct-object pronoun. No Spanish substitute text detected.
Standard Basque syntax and technical vocabulary are defensible. Long clauses retain the source implications; no certain error identified.
Maltese script, articles, inflection and technical loans are coherent. The HTML split s-sid preserves the assimilated article and owner noun.
Georgian Mkhedruli and polite UI constructions are coherent. Repaired overly specific connection quantity; no other source-meaning error found.
Kyrgyz-specific Cyrillic and morphology are present. Repaired connection count; technical register and fluent idiom remain review priorities.
Tatar Cyrillic and distinctive Turkic grammar are coherent. Repaired connection count. Additional idiom/technical terminology review is useful.
Montenegrin Latin/Ijekavian profile is consistent, including permissible ś in pośetite. Shared wording with neighboring standards is expected and not itself a translation error.
Serbian Latin/Ekavian rendering preserves the source meanings and standard diacritics/digraphs. This is a script profile rather than a new language identity.

Readable modern Scots with consistent ye/tae/noo/cannae and other Scots forms. Technical terms and whole short headings shared with English are not automatically omissions; Scots lacks a single universally imposed technical orthography.
Macedonian Cyrillic grammar and definite forms are coherent; no source-meaning error found.

Neo-Latin technical register is transparent and agreement generally sound. Added the explicit reflexive object in the connection clause. This is practical modern Latin, not a claim of a Vatican-approved technical glossary.

Independently read all strings against English and cnr Latin. Correct Cyrillic rendering retains Ijekavian/Montenegrin wording, including љ/њ/ђ/ћ and с + combining acute for ś in both occurrences of pośetite. A separate character-level reverse check reproduced every Latin leaf. ASCII identifiers, URLs, HTML and placeholders remain untouched; no stray Latin prose was found. This is a script profile of cnr, not an extra language identity.
languageAssessments.sourceAccessNote: Government orthography hosted by University of Montenegro found in indexed primary text; direct PDF fetch returned 502.

limitations: No native-speaker certification is claimed. Reviewer confidence is lower for gd, ky, tt, sco and la than for the strongest profiles.

Current files preserve availability rather than existence, source/origin-server meanings, elapsed time limits, excess request flooding, abnormal connections without accusing an attack, the JavaScript recommendation, and expected maintenance return.
The four original drafting issues and the additional Latin refinement were discussed with the author before applying them.
